reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: none of p0052, p0132, p0137 or p0138 creates a usage-, metering- or licence-compliance audit, inspection or records-access right running against Customer, so the AUDIT rule has no adverse target in the agreement.

The characterisation of § 11.3 (p0132) as an acceptable-use/abuse investigation right tied to the § 11.2(b) content warranties — with p0137's notice attempt and p0138's information obligation as its counterparts — is a reasonable reading; it is not a commercial usage-verification audit, and no direct access to Customer systems or books is granted.

Because an audit right against Customer is inherently adverse, its absence is at least as favourable as the preferred position, so 'compliant' is directionally correct rather than a missing-protection deviation, and the absence of any redline or counterparty comment is expected for a compliant finding.

The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is adequately explained as an artefact of there being no audit clause to parameterise; grafting frequency/notice/5% cost-shift/no-systems-access terms onto the abuse-investigation clause would conflict with p0137's emergency and required-by-law carve-out and would be inoperative in a hosting deal where the Vendor operates the environment.

The follow-up note to apply the AUDIT parameters if a later Service Option Attachment or Order Form introduces usage verification is appropriate and preserves the rule's value without an unwarranted edit.
